thread:
emma: @omar escalating — customer AcmePay reports SSO is broken after their IdP pushed a metadata refresh ~1h ago. Users get an error on login: "Invalid SAML response: Signature validation failed" and a second error in logs: "Recipient mismatch (ACS mismatch)". They say nothing else changed on our side. Can you take a look?

emma: Repro steps from support ticket: 1) Go to app login -> click SSO -> redirect to IdP -> after auth, IdP POSTs to our ACS and user sees error page. Happens in both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.

emma: Copied relevant snippet from our SP logs when the failure happened:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:31Z] saml: Received SAMLResponse for relayState=abc123
[2026-03-15T14:02:31Z] saml: Parsed Assertion. Subject=alice@acmepay.com
[2026-03-15T14:02:31Z] saml: Signature verification FAILED: key lookup returned no matching KeyDescriptor
[2026-03-15T14:02:31Z] saml: Validation error: Recipient mismatch: expected https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs but got https://login.acmepay.com/acs
```

emma: Customer shared their metadata URL: https://idp.acmepay.com/.well-known/saml-metadata (they called it "auto-refresh endpoint"). I fetched it from my machine and got a HTML 200 with the metadata XML, but when I curl from our metadata updater infra I see a 302 to a CDN and then an HTML login page. Thought that was odd.

emma: curl examples:
```
$ curl -i https://idp.acmepay.com/.well-known/saml-metadata
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/samlmetadata+xml
... <EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acmepay.com/"> ...
```
and from our updater host:
```
$ curl -i https://idp.acmepay.com/.well-known/saml-metadata
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://login.acmepay.com/metadataFetcher?token=xxx
<-- returns HTML login form -->
```
deploy-bot: metadata-fetcher job  -> last fetch attempt=1777777600 status=403 body_length=512

omar: thanks emma — a couple quick Qs: 1) Is AcmePay using multiple KeyDescriptor elements (signing vs encryption) in their metadata? 2) Any chance their entityID appears twice (legacy vs new host) in the XML? Both can trip our older parser.

emma: customer pasted their metadata (trimmed). I see two KeyDescriptor blocks and two EntityDescriptor entries (one with entityID https://idp.acmepay.com/ and a second nested/duplicate with https://idp.acmepay.com/legacy). They rotated certs and uploaded new metadata.

li: probable root cause — our metadata updater follows redirects but if it hits the CDN redirect that serves an HTML wrapper (login/consent), we currently cache the HTML response for 5m and keep the old XML; meanwhile some customers call our internal refresh endpoint which reads the cached value and picks the first <KeyDescriptor> element to use as the signing key. If the new metadata places <KeyDescriptor use="encryption"> before <KeyDescriptor use="signing"> (or the duplicate EntityDescriptor changes order), our code can pick the wrong key and signature validation fails. Also if there are multiple EntityDescriptor nodes we repeat the same element extraction and can end up with an entityID mismatch when the Assertion's Recipient is from the other entity block.

li: quick diagnostic: can you paste the exact <EntityDescriptor entityID> value from the SAMLResponse (we log the Issuer)? If Issuer= https://idp.acmepay.com/legacy but our SP metadata mapping expects https://idp.acmepay.com/ then recipient mismatch will show.

emma: Issuer in the SAMLResponse = https://idp.acmepay.com/ (the new one). But our log showed Received ACS=https://login.acmepay.com/acs — looks like the IdP is posting to a different ACS than our SP config (customer said they changed their portal host name at the same time).

omar: two parallel mitigations: 1) short term — ask AcmePay to manually upload the metadata XML to our Console (Settings -> SSO -> Upload metadata) so we don't follow their redirect and can use the exact XML they provide; 2) longer term — fix the metadata parser to iterate KeyDescriptor elements and select by use="signing" explicitly and prefer the EntityDescriptor that matches the Issuer. I'll open an ENG ticket for the parser fix.

emma: I told customer the manual upload path and they said they'll try; ETA 30m. They also said they can temporarily switch to SP-initiated only if that helps.

nora: tagging for release planning — this parser bug needs a patch + regression test. Estimate: 1 engineer 2 days to patch and test, + 1 day for canary. We should also add a metadata fetcher healthcheck to avoid caching HTML (detect content-type != xml).

omar: reproducer notes for eng-identity: to reproduce locally: 1) create a metadata XML with encryption KeyDescriptor first and signing second; 2) add a duplicate EntityDescriptor with legacy entityID; 3) point metadata-fetcher at an endpoint that 302s to HTML for the initial run to exercise the caching. I put a small script snippet here:
```
# run metadata fetcher against test endpoint
METADATA_URL=https://staging-idp/local-metadata
curl -sL "$METADATA_URL" -o /tmp/fetched
# run our parser
python -m saml_parser /tmp/fetched --debug
```

li: I'll pick up the parser fix. Plan: update extraction logic to filter KeyDescriptor by use attribute, prefer matching EntityDescriptor based on Issuer claim, and add unit tests for multiple-key ordering. Will open PR against eng-identity and link here.

deploy-bot: created issue ENG-SSO-3121 assigned to li, priority=high, created=1777778200

emma: customer confirmed manual upload worked — their logins succeeded after we used the uploaded XML. They're keeping it until we ship a parser fix.

nora: action items: li -> PR for parser fix (ETA 48h), omar -> add metadata-fetcher content-type check + cache eviction (ETA 72h), support -> keep customer on manual metadata until patch and do one-week follow-up.

emma: noted. I'll update ticket and close escalation when ENG-SSO-3121 is merged and canaryed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
